Danites
DAN-ites
n. pl.
The descendants of Dan, Jacob’s son by Bilhah, whose name means judge. Assigned a lot on the Philistine border they never held, they migrated north, took Laish by the sword, renamed it Dan, and set up a graven image there — the first standing idolatry in Israel and the northern anchor of Jeroboam’s calves.

Biblical Definition

The Danites are Israel’s cautionary tribe. Their allotted inheritance lay on the coastal plain toward Joppa, hard against the Philistines, and they could not hold it. From Zorah and Eshtaol, of the family of the Danites, came Manoah and his barren wife and the son given them, Samson (Judges 13:2) — a judge who fought the Philistines alone because his tribe would not. Judges 18 then records what the tribe did instead: six hundred men appointed with weapons of war went north, robbed Micah of his ephod and teraphim and his hired Levite, took the quiet unsuspecting city of Laish, burned it, rebuilt it as Dan, and installed the stolen images — and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land (Judges 18:30). That sanctuary stood for centuries; Jeroboam later set one of his golden calves there. Jacob’s blessing had said, Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path (Genesis 49:17). Dan is not named among the sealed tribes of Revelation 7, though Ezekiel 48 gives Dan a portion in the restored land — and the omission has occasioned much sober comment and a good deal of unwarranted speculation.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 has no DANITE entry. The Hebrew Dan means judge, from Rachel’s word at his birth, God hath judged me (Genesis 30:6); the city of Dan gave the proverb from Dan even to Beersheba.

expand to see more

DANITE, n. — A descendant of Dan, the son of Jacob by Bilhah; one of the tribe whose lot lay toward the Philistine coast and who afterward settled at Laish in the far north.

Genesis 30:6 gives the naming: And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.

The northern city of Dan, formerly Laish or Leshem, fixed the proverbial northern limit of the land, from Dan even to Beersheba.

Samson, the tribe’s one judge, was of Zorah, of the family of the Danites (Judges 13:2).

Webster 1828 does not carry the gentilic; Joshua 19, Judges 13-18, and 1 Kings 12 supply the biblical usage.

Key Scripture

Genesis 49:17 — "Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, that biteth the horse heels, so that his rider shall fall backward."

Judges 13:2 — "And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bare not."

Judges 18:11 — "And there went from thence of the family of the Danites, out of Zorah and out of Eshtaol, six hundred men appointed with weapons of war."

Judges 18:30 — "And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land."

1 Chronicles 12:35 — "And of the Danites expert in war twenty and eight thousand and six hundred."

Modern Corruption

Dan’s absence from the sealed tribes of Revelation 7 has been made to carry an enormous weight of speculation — most notoriously the tradition that Antichrist will arise from Dan — and the text supports none of it.

expand to see more

Irenaeus reported a tradition, drawn from Jeremiah 8:16 and Genesis 49:17, that the man of sin would come out of Dan, and dispensational writers have kept it alive. Scripture nowhere says so. Revelation 7 omits Dan and lists Manasseh alongside Joseph to keep the number at twelve; the list also omits Ephraim by name. Building a doctrine of Antichrist’s ancestry on an omission is precisely the method the Reformers rejected when they insisted that Scripture interprets Scripture and that what is not plainly set down is not to be pressed on the conscience. Ezekiel 48:1 gives Dan the first portion in the restored land, which no theory of Danite reprobation can absorb.

What the text does say is worth more than the speculation. A tribe that would not fight for the inheritance God gave took an easier one by attacking a quiet people that dwelt careless, and it carried a stolen ephod and a hired priest along with it. Judges 18:30 dates the priesthood of that shrine to the captivity of the land, meaning Dan’s idolatry outlived every man who set it up. Sin planted at a tribe’s founding does not stay a founder’s sin. Jeroboam found a calf-shrine already waiting at Dan four centuries later, and the northern kingdom went into exile with it standing.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Dan (H1835), judge, from din (H1777) to judge or plead a cause; the gentilic is Dani (H1839).

expand to see more

Hebrew Dan (H1835) — Dan; a judge, from Rachel’s God hath judged me (Genesis 30:6).

Hebrew din (H1777) — to judge, to contend, to plead a cause; the root of the name.

Hebrew Dani (H1839) — Danite; Judges 13:2, 18:11, 1 Chronicles 12:35.

Hebrew Layish (H3919) — Laish, a lion; the quiet city taken and renamed Dan (Judges 18:29).

Hebrew pesel (H6459) — a graven image; the children of Dan set up the graven image (Judges 18:30).

Usage

"Dan shall be a serpent by the way (Genesis 49:17) — Jacob’s word over the tribe."

"Six hundred men appointed with weapons of war (Judges 18:11) — the migration that took an easier inheritance."

"The children of Dan set up the graven image (Judges 18:30) — a shrine that outlasted the men who built it."
